summary: A dense sci-fi civilization game where you terraform hex planets to match your species, build a network of connected outposts, and climb six research tracks for snowballing bonuses. It plays like a tighter, better-balanced sequel to Terra Mystica, with the same feeling of racing rivals up shared tech tracks while carving out territory on a modular board.
praised: clean, elegant systems for a game this deep
criticised: steep learning curve and long first plays
heavy iconography and upfront rules overhead
can feel more solitary/optimization-puzzle than confrontational
analysis paralysis in the mid-late game

interaction.kind: competing for adjacent hexes, tech-track slots and federations on a shared map
interaction.detail: Players terraform and settle a shared hex map, so proximity to opponents affects power gains and who can wall off expansion routes, and research tracks/round bonuses are a limited shared resource. But because the galaxy is large and factions inhabit different planet types, most of a turn is still spent optimizing your own tech and building chain rather than directly clashing with a neighbor.
interaction.said: unknown — often compared unfavorably to its predecessor Terra Mystica as the more 'multiplayer solitaire' of the two, with less of the adjacency-based interaction that made Terra Mystica feel tense

scoring.how_you_win: Over 6 rounds, expand your network of colonized planets, climb the six research tracks, and form federations; the player with the most combined round, final, and research VP at the end wins.
